conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — March 26, 2015 Regular Board Meeting
conflicts.summary: Following presentation of the tri-party redevelopment agreement among DPS, Durham County, and Integral Development LLC—which also noted DPS and the County would split Pre-K center operating costs equally and that further legal documents might follow—the Board split 4-3 to approve the agreement.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Whitted Project Agreement with Durham County and Integral Development LLC.
side_a_arguments: Advances planning, renovation, construction, and operation of the redeveloped Whitted facility under a tri-party public-private partnership.
Establishes equal County and DPS sharing of operating costs for the Pre-K center.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed approving the Whitted Project Agreement.
side_b_arguments: Voted Nay following thorough Board discussion (specific dissenting arguments are not detailed in the official minutes).
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-3 on a motion by Minnie Forte-Brown seconded by Matt Sears.

conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — February 26, 2015 Regular Monthly Meeting (Rescheduled To March 2)
conflicts.issue: Traditional Schools Inclement Weather Make-Up Calendar (Removing Memorial Day / Extending to June 10-11)
conflicts.summary: Following public comment debating Memorial Day, teacher workdays, early release conversions, and local assessments, the Board split 6-1 in approving the administration's Traditional Schools make-up schedule that removed Memorial Day and extended the student calendar to June 10-11.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the administration's Traditional Schools make-up schedule removing Memorial Day (May 25) and utilizing June 10, June 11, early release days, and banked instructional time.
side_a_arguments: Avoids holding school on Memorial Day, a statewide observed holiday, as recommended by administration over the Calendar Committee's initial Memorial Day proposal.
Complies with state calendar law requiring the last student day to fall no later than the Friday closest to June 11.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed the proposed Traditional Schools make-up calendar.
side_b_arguments: Voted Nay following Board discussion and public comments concerning end-of-year workdays, Memorial Day, and instructional time (specific rationale from Leigh Bordley not detailed in the minutes).
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 on a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Sendolo Diaminah; Year-Round and Modified School make-up calendars subsequently passed 7-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — January 22, 2015 Regular Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Additional $800,000 Capital Funding and 2007 Bond Transfer for Whitted Project
conflicts.summary: The Board split 6-1 over transferring $800,000 from $1.8 million in 2007 bond funds assigned to W. G. Pearson Middle School to cover increased redevelopment costs for the Whitted Building, even after amending the motion to specify that participating bodies will negotiate operating costs requiring new funding.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the additional $800,000 capital contribution from 2007 bond funds conditioned on intergovernmental negotiation of future operating costs requiring new funding.
side_a_arguments: Cost increases in the Whitted Building redevelopment require an additional $800,000 capital contribution from DPS alongside the City and County.
Administration recommended transferring the $800,000 from $1.8 million in 2007 bond funds assigned to W. G. Pearson Middle School.
The amended motion established the understanding that all participating bodies will negotiate operating costs, which will require new funding.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed the amended $800,000 capital funding and 2007 bond transfer motion for the Whitted Project.
side_b_arguments: Voted against the amended motion (minutes do not record specific spoken objections by Natalie Beyer).

conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — August 28, 2014 Regular Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Renewal of Teach for America (TFA) Contract vs. Investing in Teacher Mentoring and Career Pipelines
conflicts.summary: Following 11 public speakers (six favoring TFA renewal and five opposing), the Board split 6-1 on whether to renew a three-year TFA contract or only honor existing two-year commitments for five current corps members while shifting resources toward internal mentoring and Graduate Durham.
conflicts.side_a_position: Honor commitments for the 5 current TFA corps members ($3,000 per member for two years) but decline to renew or enter further TFA contracts, prioritizing career educators and mentoring.
side_a_arguments: TFA's five-to-six-week pre-service training without student teaching undermines teaching as a profession and is unfair to career teachers (Natalie Beyer, Dr. Mike Lee, Sendolo Diaminah).
Long-term retention is low, with Dr. Mike Lee noting only 25 of 200 past TFA hires remained teaching and speakers urging funds be redirected to mentoring beginning teachers.

Contract dollars and district focus should support Graduate Durham and a systemic career teacher pipeline while avoiding mid-year classroom disruption for current teachers (Leigh Bordley, Matt Sears, Heidi Carter).
conflicts.side_b_position: Renew the full Teach for America contract to keep staffing hard-to-fill schools.
side_b_arguments: Hard-to-staff schools risk relying on long-term substitutes when the local hiring pool is low without TFA recruitment.
Committed TFA teachers hold high expectations for students, and commitment to every child matters more than classroom longevity alone.
conflicts.resolution: Matt Sears's motion to honor existing two-year obligations for the five current TFA corps members without entering new contracts passed 6-1, and Superintendent L'Homme pledged to present an internal mentoring plan using existing staff development funds.

conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — June 25, 2015 Regular Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Board Committee Structure and Monthly Meeting Schedule (Modified Option 2)
conflicts.summary: Board members debated options for the number of monthly meetings, days of the week, and start and end times before voting 4-2 to adopt modified Option 2 establishing three monthly committee-of-the-whole meetings starting at 4:00 p.m.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support modified Option 2 establishing three monthly committee-of-the-whole meetings at 4:00 p.m. with two-hour time-boxed agendas.
side_a_arguments: Restructures monthly work into a combined Academic and Support Services meeting on the first Monday, an Operation and Visions meeting on the second Thursday, and the regular meeting on the fourth Thursday.
Operates each meeting as a committee of the whole with agenda items time-boxed (except public comment) and set by the Chair, Vice Chair, and Superintendent.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed modified Option 2 committee structure and meeting schedule.
side_b_arguments: Voted against modified Option 2 following thorough discussion of alternative options for meeting count, start/end times, and days of the week (specific dissenting rationales not detailed in the minutes).
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-2; the Board subsequently voted 6-0 to return Policy 2230 (Board Committees) to committee in August to align policy with the new format.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education — May 26, 2016 Regular Monthly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 26, 2016 Regular Monthly Meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education (with five members present and Sendolo Diaminah and Minnie Forte-Brown absent) unanimously approved the meeting agenda (5-0) and the April 2016 meeting minutes (5-0). Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme highlighted district celebrations, a $250,000 Kenan Charitable Trust grant for restorative justice work with five pilot schools through the Coalition of Schools Educating Boys of Color, and Lowe's Grove Middle School being named STEM School of the Year by Fidelity Investments. Six public speakers raised concerns about Eastway Elementary breakfast service, digital access barriers, systemic racism, and upcoming voting, while two speakers voiced opposition to North Carolina House Bill 2 (HB2). The Board reviewed two proposed 2016-2017 work session calendar schedules, deferring action to the next work session or board meeting, and received an informational legal briefing from Dr. Debbie Pitman and Board Attorney Ken Soo on federal Title IX guidance, pending HB2 litigation, and administrative guidelines for supporting transgender students.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Heidi Carter called the meeting to order at 6:33 p.m. and led a moment of silence. The Board recognized Student of the Month Ryan Bunn (Hillside New Tech), Counselors of the Year, Beginning Teachers of the Year, Transportation Drivers and Monitors of the Year, National Board Certified Teachers, 18 four-year straight-A high school seniors, Gates Millennium and Coca-Cola scholars, Congressional District Arts Award winner Rene Chavez Lopez, the 4A state champion Hillside High School boys track team, and NCAE Principal of the Year Dr. William Logan.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme recognized Teacher of the Year Justine Daniel (Githens Middle), the retirement banquet, and graduations for Early College, CMA, and Middle College. He announced a $250,000 Kenan Charitable Trust grant for the Coalition of Schools Educating Boys of Color to pilot restorative justice practices in five schools starting January 2017, Lowe's Grove Middle School's STEM Scholars Dream Book and Fidelity Investments STEM School of the Year award, and student Bettie Closs placing in the final 17 at the National Spelling Bee.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed the meeting agenda for the May 26, 2016 regular monthly meeting with five members present.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six speakers addressed the Board: Sheryl Smith and Anita Keith-Foust raised concerns regarding Eastway Elementary breakfast service and public reliance on online information; Donna Rewalt spoke on behalf of the Cooperative Extension Parents as Leaders Program and thanked Natalie Beyer; James Chavis shared a PAC and Mayor's Poverty Initiative Committee handout; Rhonda Bullock addressed systemic racism and announced summer programs at Hillside High; and Dr. Allison encouraged turnout for the June 7 election.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 2016 Board of Education Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes for the April 18, 2016 Public Hearing Work Session, April 20, 2016 Magnet Schools Update Work Session, and April 28, 2016 Regular Monthly Meeting.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two proposed 2016-2017 Schedule of Board of Education Meetings calendars were presented ('Tuesdays - Thursdays' and 'Thursdays Only'). No public speakers signed up on this item, and the Board decided to bring the calendar schedule back to the next work session or board meeting without taking a vote.

Gloucester County School Board decision, pending federal lawsuits involving HB2, and day-to-day school practices covering transition support teams, NCHSAA athletics rules, extracurriculars, bullying prevention, dress code, and student records.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education — April 18, 2016 Public Hearing &Amp; 16 17 Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 18, 2016 Public Hearing and Budget Work Session (with five members present and Leigh Bordley and Dr. Mike Lee absent), the Board unanimously approved a revised agenda (5-0) removing the word 'approval' from line item 5. Eleven members of the public addressed the Board regarding the FY 2016-2017 budget, prompting Chair Heidi Carter to attribute staffing pressures to state funding cuts. Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme reported that 91.5 positions had been eliminated—primarily through Central Services reductions, combined roles, and Exceptional Children department restructuring—while confirming that no Exceptional Children Instructional Assistants would be cut. Board members Matt Sears, Minnie Forte-Brown, and Natalie Beyer discussed operating versus capital bond funding and teacher retention pressures, and the Board directed Dr. L'Homme to restore the Teacher Mentor program in the budget proposal for the April 28, 2016 meeting.

Chair Carter thanked parents for their comments, stated that all eliminated positions add value to DPS, and criticized state cuts for dismantling public education.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services and Policy Work Session: 2016-2017 Budget Development Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme reported that no Exceptional Children Instructional Assistants would be cut, though 91.5 positions were eliminated across Central Services and operations through job consolidation and EC departmental reorganization, noting more decisions could return in August. Matt Sears and Minnie Forte-Brown clarified differences between operating revenue and capital bond funds, Natalie Beyer urged a resolution for increased per-pupil funding to recruit and retain teachers, and the Board charged the Superintendent to add the Teacher Mentor program back into the budget for April 28, 2016.

meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present on February 25, 2016, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved an amended agenda (7-0), the January 28, 2016 meeting minutes (7-0), the Consent Agenda (7-0), a closed session motion for personnel and litigation consultation (7-0), and the February 25, 2016 Personnel Reports (7-0). Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme reported that the Code of Student Conduct Task Force recommended revising Policy 4301 to allow cultural and educational dress code accommodations such as the gele, announced DPS and Durham Tech were finalists for a $600,000 Cooperative Innovative High Schools grant, and detailed Black History Month school activities. Ten public speakers addressed mandatory Black History instruction, employee speech rights, the Code of Student Conduct, and the FY 2016-2017 budget. Under Reports of the Board, members reviewed two competing drafts of a Resolution in Support of Employee Speech Rights—an initial First Amendment draft and a revised version from Board Attorney Ken Soo—and agreed to return the resolution to the next work session for further review without taking a vote.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education — January 28, 2016 Regular Monthly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 28, 2016 Regular Monthly Meeting (with six members present and Sendolo Diaminah absent), Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme warned that DPS faced a $9 million baseline budget gap—plus up to $3 million more if state-mandated 5% certified and 3% classified pay raises required local matching funds—while introducing a consolidated district improvement plan targeting third-grade reading, eighth-grade math and reading, and graduation rates. Five public speakers advocated for mandatory Black History instruction in DPS schools and raised discipline and budget concerns. The Board unanimously approved the agenda by common consent (6-0), December 17 and January 13 minutes (6-0), the Consent Agenda with Leigh Bordley's custodial contract addition requiring windows to remain closed (6-0), a Resolution Supporting January 2016 as National Mentor Month (6-0), and revised Board Policy 2475 on School Rules (6-0). Following an informational presentation on the 2015-2017 District Improvement Plan, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session (6-0) and subsequently approved the January 28, 2016 Personnel Reports (6-0).

Powe Elementary), and Community Partner the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

He previewed a consolidated district improvement plan focused on third-grade reading, eighth-grade math and reading, graduation rates, operational efficiencies, and district culture.

Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme paid tribute to former Durham City Schools administrator and DPS Athletic Director Willie Bradshaw and celebrated district student and educator honors, while DAE President Andrea Petifer urged the Board to join NCAE Lobby Days against state per-pupil funding shortfalls. Under the Administrative Services Committee, the Board split 4-3 to approve the public-private Whitted Project Agreement with Durham County and Integral Development LLC (Ayes: Heidi Carter, Minnie Forte-Brown, Matt Sears, Leigh Bordley; Nays: Sendolo Diaminah, Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer), after reviewing a presentation noting the County and DPS would split operating costs for the Pre-K center equally. CFO Aaron Beaulieu also presented an informational 2015-2016 budget development update, and the Board unanimously entered closed session (7-0) and approved the March 26, 2015 Personnel Reports (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Be Our Guest, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Heidi Carter called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. and led a moment of silence. Matt Sears welcomed families from five schools, and Chief Communications Officer Chrissy Pearson recognized Students of the Month Bakari Smith (Hillside High) and Kailey Morgan (DSA), Backpack Buddies donor Aahron Benthall (Pearsontown), two-time Duke Regional Spelling Bee champion Bettie Closs (Lucas Middle), and 32 National Board Certified Teachers (21 newly certified, 11 renewed).

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Bert L'Homme reflected on attending the funeral of Willie Bradshaw, Durham City Schools' first African American administrator and DPS's first Athletic Director after merger, thanked the Board for its Brogden Junior High integration resolution, and highlighted Hillside basketball standout Justine Lyon, Title I Engineering Night, Dacia Jones's SXSWedu panel, and City Human Rights Youth Award winners.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The agenda was approved as written by common consent. One public speaker, Pearsontown Assistant Principal and DAE President Andrea Petifer, highlighted North Carolina ranking 46th nationally in per-pupil spending and Governor McCrory's proposed budget, urging Board members to join NCAE Lobby Days in Raleigh on April 28 and June 23.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the February 26 (rescheduled to March 2) and March 16, 2015 minutes (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Sendolo Diaminah) and a six-item Consent Agenda covering a Hope Valley easement, Hillandale roofing and kitchen/life-safety/site upgrades, Githens athletic fields, Brogden life-safety upgrades, and Southwest life-safety upgrades (moved by Sendolo Diaminah, seconded by Minnie Forte-Brown).

agenda_items.title: Administrative Services Committee: Whitted Project Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Hugh Osteen presented the public-private partnership agreement among DPS, Durham County, and Integral Development LLC for renovation, construction, and operation of the redeveloped Whitted facility, noting DPS and the County would share Pre-K center operating costs equally. Following thorough discussion, Minnie Forte-Brown moved approval and Matt Sears seconded, passing 4-3 with Sendolo Diaminah, Dr. Mike Lee, and Natalie Beyer voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Services Committee: 2015-2016 Budget Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron Beaulieu reviewed Board-approved budget priorities and guiding principles, fixed-cost and state-mandate projections, and potential use of lapse salary dollars as staff prepared a balanced local current expense budget for submission to County Commissioners by May 15, 2015.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee and second by Natalie Beyer, the Board entered closed session at 8:15 p.m. under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6), 115C-319, and 143-318.11(a)(3). Reconvening at 8:59 p.m., the Board unanimously approved the March 26, 2015 Personnel Reports before adjourning at 9:00 p.m.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education — January 22, 2015 Regular Monthly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 22, 2015 regular monthly meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme's updates, including a formal statement criticizing North Carolina's forthcoming school performance letter-grade formula for emphasizing proficiency over student academic growth. The Board unanimously approved (7-0) its consent agenda—covering an alternative school accountability model, chiller replacement bids for Forest View and Oak Grove Elementary Schools, Eastway Elementary right-of-ways/easements, and policy revisions—as well as a $100,000 current-fiscal-year allocation to support the Made In Durham initiative and the January 22, 2015 personnel reports. On the meeting's sole contested item, the Board voted 6-1 to approve an amended motion providing an additional $800,000 in capital funding for the Whitted Building redevelopment project by transferring funds from $1.8 million in 2007 bond funds previously assigned to W. G. Pearson Middle School, with the understanding that all participating governing bodies will negotiate operating costs requiring new funding; Heidi Carter, Dr. Mike Lee, Minnie Forte-Brown, Leigh Bordley, Matt Sears, and Sendolo Diaminah voted Aye, while Natalie Beyer voted Nay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Be Our Guest, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Heidi Carter called the meeting to order and presided over a moment of silence, noting Vice Chair Minnie Forte-Brown was attending via conference call from the NCSBA Policy Conference. Dr. Mike Lee thanked Northern High School culinary students and joined the Board and Superintendent in recognizing parents and guardians from six DPS schools. Chief Communications Officer Chrissy Pearson recognized January Duke University DPS Student of the Month Jose Leno Morales of Durham Performance Learning Center, along with community partners Biogen Idec and the Assistance League of the Triangle Area.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Updates and School Performance Grades Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme thanked Board members for School Board Appreciation Month, reviewed recent inclement weather delays and Winter Graduation scheduling, and highlighted regional and state honors for DPS educators and student opportunities. He then read a formal statement criticizing the state's upcoming February 5 release of school performance letter grades, noting that 37 DPS schools meeting or exceeding growth expectations could receive Ds or Fs under a proficiency-heavy formula. Sendolo Diaminah announced a February 5 community conversation on school letter grades at Riverside High School.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, General Public Comment, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the meeting agenda and four sets of prior meeting minutes from December 2014 and January 2015 by common consent. During general public comment, parent Kim Harris raised concerns regarding an incident involving her daughter at Hillandale Elementary and a pending change in her homebound teacher, to which Chair Carter responded that administration would follow up. Durham Association of Educators President Andrea Underwood Petifer spoke in support of the Board's resolution opposing state school letter grades and promoted the February 5 community conversation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Carter noted that all six Consent Agenda items had been thoroughly discussed in committee. The items included the Alternative School Accountability Model, bids for chiller replacements at Forest View Elementary School and Oak Grove Elementary School, right-of-ways and easement at Eastway Elementary School, DPS Policy Manual revisions with the NCSBA, and Revised Policy 3300 on student access to high school courses.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Services Committee: Additional Capital Funding for the Whitted Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Hugh Osteen presented a request for DPS, alongside the City and County, to contribute additional capital due to cost increases in redeveloping the Whitted Building, recommending transferring $800,000 from $1.8 million in 2007 bond funds assigned to W. G. Pearson Middle School. After Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Leigh Bordley seconded the initial recommendation, Board members discussed the proposal and agreed to amend the motion. Sendolo Diaminah moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded an amended motion approving the $800,000 transfer with the understanding that all governing bodies will negotiate operating costs requiring new funding.

agenda_items.title: Support Services Committee: Made In Durham Funding Allocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent L'Homme, CTE Director Rick Sheldahl, and Made In Durham representatives David Dodson and Julie Mooney presented the Made In Durham initiative supporting disconnected youth and young adults toward postsecondary credentials and living wages by age 25. Administration recommended spending $100,000 for Made In Durham, with an additional $100,000 in year two contingent on meeting benchmarks. Following Board discussion, Leigh Bordley moved and Natalie Beyer seconded allocating $100,000 in the current fiscal year.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At approximately 8:12 p.m., upon request by Board Attorney Ken Soo to add statutory student confidentiality citations, the Board voted on a motion by Leigh Bordley and second by Natalie Beyer to enter closed session for confidential student, personnel, and attorney-client matters. The Board reconvened in open session at approximately 8:57 p.m. and unanimously approved the January 22, 2015 Personnel Reports before adjourning at 8:59 p.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — August 28, 2014 Regular Monthly Meeting
disagreements.issue: Renewal of Teach for America (TFA) Contract vs. Investing in Teacher Mentoring and Career Pipelines
disagreements.summary: Following 11 public speakers (six favoring TFA renewal and five opposing), the Board split 6-1 on whether to renew a three-year TFA contract or only honor existing two-year commitments for five current corps members while shifting resources toward internal mentoring and Graduate Durham.
disagreements.side_a_position: Honor commitments for the 5 current TFA corps members ($3,000 per member for two years) but decline to renew or enter further TFA contracts, prioritizing career educators and mentoring.
side_a_arguments: TFA's five-to-six-week pre-service training without student teaching undermines teaching as a profession and is unfair to career teachers (Natalie Beyer, Dr. Mike Lee, Sendolo Diaminah).
Long-term retention is low, with Dr. Mike Lee noting only 25 of 200 past TFA hires remained teaching and speakers urging funds be redirected to mentoring beginning teachers.

Contract dollars and district focus should support Graduate Durham and a systemic career teacher pipeline while avoiding mid-year classroom disruption for current teachers (Leigh Bordley, Matt Sears, Heidi Carter).
disagreements.side_b_position: Renew the full Teach for America contract to keep staffing hard-to-fill schools.
side_b_arguments: Hard-to-staff schools risk relying on long-term substitutes when the local hiring pool is low without TFA recruitment.
Committed TFA teachers hold high expectations for students, and commitment to every child matters more than classroom longevity alone.
disagreements.resolution: Matt Sears's motion to honor existing two-year obligations for the five current TFA corps members without entering new contracts passed 6-1, and Superintendent L'Homme pledged to present an internal mentoring plan using existing staff development funds.

meetings.executive_summary: At the July 7, 2014 Organizational and Regular Monthly Meeting (with six members present and Leigh Bordley absent due to a medical emergency), newly elected and re-elected Board members Dr. Mike Lee, Sendolo Diaminah, Matt Sears, and Natalie Beyer took the Oath of Office administered by Chief District Court Judge Marcia H. Morey. The Board unanimously elected Heidi Carter as Chair (6-0) and Minnie Forte-Brown as Vice Chair (6-0) by acclamation before transitioning to the regular monthly session at 11:21 a.m. After approving the agenda by consent (6-0) and hearing two public speakers on school waste reduction and Lowe's Grove Middle School test scores, Chair Carter announced 2014-2015 Standing Committee appointments and the Board unanimously adopted the Draft 1 schedule of monthly and standing committee meetings (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Organizational Meeting: Swearing In, Oath of Office, and Officer Elections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Stacey Wilson-Norman called the organizational meeting to order at 11:00 a.m. in Interim Superintendent Hugh Osteen's absence, and Judge Marcia H. Morey administered the Oath of Office to Dr. Mike Lee (District 1), Sendolo Diaminah (District 2), Matt Sears (District 3), and Natalie Beyer (District 4). The Board unanimously elected Heidi Carter as Chair and Minnie Forte-Brown as Vice Chair by acclamation, and Chair Carter outlined district priorities ahead of incoming Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme's arrival.

agenda_items.title: Regular Monthly Meeting: Agenda Review and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Opening the regular meeting at 11:21 a.m., the Board approved the agenda by common consent. Two speakers addressed the Board: Crystal Dreisbach (Don't Waste Durham) invited collaboration on school waste reduction—with Chair Carter noting the Board had just approved a Director of Sustainability—and Donna Frederick raised concerns regarding test scores at Lowe's Grove Middle School.

agenda_items.title: Standing Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Carter announced 2014-2015 standing committee assignments balanced across experience, race, gender, and interest: Administrative Services (Chair Natalie Beyer, Vice Chair Mike Lee, Leigh Bordley, Matt Sears), Instructional Services (Chair Minnie Forte-Brown, Vice Chair Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Sendolo Diaminah), and Support Services (Chair Leigh Bordley, Vice Chair Sendolo Diaminah, Minnie Forte-Brown, Mike Lee), with Chair Carter serving ex officio on each five-member committee.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of 2014-2015 Schedule of Board of Education Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed two proposed 2014-2015 meeting schedules—Draft 1 retaining 4:30 p.m. Standing Committee meetings and Draft 2 replacing them with 2:00 p.m. Board Work Sessions—and unanimously adopted Draft 1 before adjourning at approximately 11:36 a.m.

votes.item_title: Election of Heidi Carter as Board of Education Chair by Acclamation
votes.notes: Leigh Bordley was absent due to a medical emergency. Dr. Stacey Wilson-Norman presided until the gavel passed to Chair Carter.
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer nominated Heidi Carter for Chair; with no other nominations, the Board accepted the nomination by acclamation.

votes.item_title: Election of Minnie Forte-Brown as Board of Education Vice Chair by Acclamation
votes.notes: Leigh Bordley was absent due to a medical emergency.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee nominated Minnie Forte-Brown for Vice Chair; with no other nominations, the Board accepted the nomination by acclamation.

votes.notes: Leigh Bordley was absent; mover and seconder not named.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the regular monthly meeting agenda by common consent.
